A.summary: The original with Australian spelling only; no translation.

meaning.evidence: Every rule kept: "TDY travel is longer than 12 hours and needs a pre-approved authorisation in Concur", "travel ends when you check in at the hotel or get home", "runs out one year (26 pay periods) after you earn it".

sense.evidence: Plain swaps fit: "getting to and from work" for commuting, "work out the breakdown", "Once you hit the expiry date", "took off and landed".

authenticity.evidence: Natural plain Australian English: "Have a look at OPM's [Travel Comp Time Fact Sheet]", "Please get in touch with your Timekeeper", "expiry date".

register.evidence: A shade light even for level 2: casual plain English with "Have a look", "check out", "work out", "expiry", but nothing distinctively Aussie.

tone.evidence: Stays a clear, helpful HR page: "If you leave GSA, any unused travel comp time is lost."

flow.evidence: Smooth throughout: "Use the time zone where you departed from to work out elapsed time." (a small "where ... from" redundancy).

variety.evidence: "work out" three times ("to work out the breakdown", "For working out", "to work out elapsed time"); otherwise little slang to vary.

essence.evidence: Clearly the TTS comp-time policy, every section kept.

B.summary: A faithful, natural plain-English Australian version, a touch light on Aussie colour.

meaning.evidence: Every rule kept, with a helpful gloss: "travel comp time (time in lieu for travel)", "needs an authorisation approved beforehand in Concur", "expires one year (26 pay periods) after you earn it".

sense.evidence: Terms fit: "time in lieu" is the Australian workplace term for comp time, "normal working hours", "have a chat to your Timekeeper", "GSA staff".

authenticity.evidence: Sounds like an Australian HR page: "time in lieu for travel", "If you've got questions, have a chat to your Timekeeper or an HR Specialist at your agency."

register.evidence: Level 2: a light, natural touch with "time in lieu", "have a chat to", "staff"; no swearing.

tone.evidence: Clear, helpful HR tone kept: "If you leave GSA, any travel comp time you haven't used is forfeited."

flow.evidence: Smooth: "Travelling during your usual work day counts as normal hours, and that includes travelling from home to the airport."

variety.evidence: "normal" four times and "work out" twice; light touch otherwise varied.

essence.evidence: Clearly the TTS policy, every section kept.
